title: ComCat shallow-depth share rose 5.20 points more than GCMT centroid share for matched M5.8+ events in 2005-2020
abstract: We compared two depth measures for 3,734 matched earthquakes at ComCat preferred M >=5.8. Between 2005-2012 and 2013-2020, the fraction at depth 15 km or less rose by 5.39 percentage points in ComCat and by 0.18 points for Global CMT centroid depths. The paired change difference was 5.20 points, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of 1.77 to 8.51 points. Fixed broad location and magnitude weights gave a 5.20-point difference. Tight matching and 20 and 30 km cuts retained positive differences. A FREE-only centroid sample gave an uncertain 3.07-point difference. Matching controls event identity but does not make the depth measures equivalent or fully independent. Origin depth describes rupture start, while centroid depth describes moment release. This result does not identify physical shallowing or the cause of the catalog difference. Short eras, catalog errors, event clustering and selected cutoffs limit inference. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a separate matching audit, repeat checks and a figure. External source records and joined event tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Annual shallow-event fractions for the same matched events, and paired era-change differences. Bars give conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Filters change the target population.
